_about: Papers, inks and process constants for printlab (Python engine/printlab/press.py and web/lib/printlab.js read this file). Lengths in mm unless named _um. Each entry says where its numbers came from: MEAS = measured by engine/printlab/measure.py (measured.json), LIT = published figure, EST = estimate.

book1874.why: MEAS paper of the Page 1874 specimen (median of the paper areas, L* 89, b* +10: aged wove book paper); texture EST

rag.why: EST cotton rag for letterpress (soft, takes impression)

whatman.why: MEAS paper of the Atkins cyanotype (Met 285421), 99th-percentile L*: 1850s writing paper as it is now (aged, toned)

poster.why: EST poster board (WPA silkscreen posters were printed on board / heavy stock)

supercal.why: EST supercalendered magazine stock of a 1920s rotogravure supplement (smooth, cream, aged)

black1874.why: MEAS solid black wood-type letters, Page 1874 p24 (density rel. paper)

blue1874.why: MEAS solid blue letters, Page 1874 p5

green1874.why: MEAS solid green letters, Page 1874 p6

prussian.why: MEAS Prussian blue at Dmax, Atkins cyanotype (Met 285421)

sepia_gravure.why: EST brown-black gravure ink; Dmax ~1.8 on supercalendered stock (LIT: gravure's deep blacks)

green_gravure.why: EST the green-black of 1920s-30s gravure supplements

riso_black.why: EST riso black on bond (soy ink is not deep: D ~1.3)

screen_ochre.why: EST opaque poster ochre (WPA-style oil-based screen ink)

letterpress.why: MEAS mottle: Page 1874 solids D sd 0.09-0.10 at 3.9 mm correlation (sd/D ~7%); LIT squash 0.05-0.1 mm; EST film and starvation

riso.why: LIT master 300 dpi (some 600); drum-to-drum drift up to ~1 mm

silkscreen.why: LIT mesh 110-200 threads/inch; EST thread fraction and deposit variation

cyanotype.why: MEAS Dmax and colour (Atkins); EST dose constant

gravure.why: LIT 150-175 lines/in, cells of equal area and variable depth; EST wall width and missing-dot threshold
